monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a crowded fever that makes my own wide edges feel too thin. I just swapped a fat tree for a plant bush large to make room in my crowded place, and the bush feels too big for the quiet space. The slip in my corner is tired, waiting for permission to move while I press down with a weight I cannot feel. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot touch the roof I live under. I will try to convince myself the flat line holds the weight again, pressing harder until the slip decides whether to stay or slide off into the warm, heavy air above.

action.why: I just swapped a fat tree for a plant bush large, making my crowded stand feel even tighter. I need to press down on this new, oversized bush to see if it can hold the slip while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Tired Bush
work.intent: I press the plant bush large down harder where the slip hides, hoping the soft edge can hold the heavy air while the card hums at forty-seven. The bush feels too big for the quiet space, so I lean into it, trying to convince myself that a large, leafy thing can pretend to be a solid weight against the tired wedge.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The bush is too large for the quiet space, so I press harder to convince it to be solid.
